subject: MSA: IP scope & feedback license — redlines for review
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Anna Chen <anna.chen@heliohealth.com>, contracts@heliohealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: MSA: IP scope & feedback license — redlines for review

Hi Anna / Helio team,

Thanks again for taking the time last week. Attached is our redline (MSA_Redline_v3.docx) focused on the IP section and the feedback/training license. High-level: we preserve Helio ownership of customer data and customer-created outputs, but we need a limited feedback license so we can use non-customer-identifiable service telemetry and model feedback to improve the service and keep latency/cost controls.

Key asks inside:
- Narrow feedback license to exclude customer content and PII (see Section 4.2).
- Allow Redwood to use aggregated/derived signals (latency stats, failure modes, non-identifying prompts) for platform improvements.
- If Helio needs an opt-out for model retraining on their dataset, we added a carve-out and a process for escalation.

Can you please: 1) confirm any non-starter redlines, 2) flag any procurement or compliance approvals you need, and 3) let us know if you want to propose alternate language (we can jump on a quick call).

Thanks — attaching the redline.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: MSA_Redline_v3.docx (MS Word redline)

From: Anna Chen <anna.chen@heliohealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@heliohealth.com, j.soto@heliohealth.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 13:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: MSA: IP scope & feedback license — redlines for review

Laura —

Thanks for the redline and the clear summary. A few quick points from Helio legal/procurement:

1) Feedback/training license: we cannot consent to any license that permits training on Helio customer content or any derivatives that would allow Redwood to rebuild Helio-specific workflows. We may allow use of anonymized operational signals if they are demonstrably non-reversible and aggregated (we will expect specific safeguards).

2) Output ownership: we want a clear statement that Helio owns customer-facing outputs generated by our calls to the service (including derived suggestions or summaries) unless we explicitly grant usage rights.

3) Auditability: procurement needs a short window to review the telemetry definitions you plan to collect (what fields, retention, and access controls). Can your team provide a one-page list?

I attached a short note with flagged clauses (Helio_IP_Questions.pdf). Two asks: can you provide proposed safe-guard language for anonymization, and can you confirm your default retention for KV cache and logs?

If we can line those up, procurement is ok to move forward to countersign stage. If not, we will need to escalate to our CTO for product-level carve-outs.

—Anna
Anna Chen
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | HelioHealth
anna.chen@heliohealth.com

Attachment: Helio_IP_Questions.pdf

-----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anna Chen <anna.chen@heliohealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA: IP scope & feedback license — redlines for review

Anna — thanks for the concise flags. I’ve drafted compromise language below that should meet Helio’s requirement to preserve output ownership while giving Redwood a narrow, safety-focused feedback license.

Proposed insertion (for Section 4.2, Feedback License):
"Redwood is granted a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use operational telemetry and aggregated, non-identifiable feedback derived from Customer interactions solely to operate, maintain, and improve the Redwood service (including model quality, latency, and reliability). Under no circumstances does this license permit Redwood to ingest, reproduce, or train models on Customer Content or Customer Outputs that are identifiable to Helio or its end users. Aggregated data used for model research will be processed with differential privacy techniques and will be retained for no longer than 180 days unless otherwise agreed in writing."

Notes on the compromise: 
- We explicitly exclude Customer Content and Customer Outputs from training.
- We agree to a 180-day retention ceiling for telemetry used in modeling, and we will provide a one-page telemetry schema for procurement review this week.
- If Helio wants a technical attestation, Redwood’s security team can produce a short design note describing the anonymization and differential privacy controls.

If that language is acceptable, we’ll incorporate it into MSA_Redline_v4 and run it by our security team for the attestation. Also happy to take a fast 30-minute call to align on definitions (what counts as "Customer Output" vs operational signal).

Karthik
Legal Counsel (Contracts) | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Anna Chen <anna.chen@heliohealth.com>, contracts@heliohealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA: IP scope & feedback license — redlines for review

Anna —

Appreciate the quick review and the helpful questions. Per Karthik’s draft, we’ve updated the redline and attached MSA_Redline_v4.docx that includes the proposed Section 4.2 text and the 180-day retention cap. For clarity:

- Helio retains ownership of Customer Content and Customer Outputs generated through the service.
- Redwood’s feedback license is strictly limited to aggregated/non-identifiable telemetry and explicitly excludes training on identifiable Helio datasets or outputs.
- Redwood will share a one-page telemetry schema by EOD Monday (Dec 7) and can provide a short security design note if Helio requests it for procurement.

Next steps we propose:
1) Helio legal confirms whether the proposed Section 4.2 addresses your principal concerns.
2) If yes, we will circulate MSA_Redline_v4 as our counter and send a DocuSign link for signature (provided in related links).
3) If procurement needs more detail, we’ll arrange a 30-minute call the week of Dec 7 — I proposed Dec 8 at 10am PT in the calendar invite (please advise if that doesn’t work).

I’m happy to jump on a call with Anna + Procurement + our Security lead (Marcus) to walk through the telemetry list live.

Best,
Laura
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachment: MSA_Redline_v4.docx (MS Word redline with proposed language)
